one_month_reasoning: The one big event in the window is TI's Q3 2026 report and Q4 guidance, expected around Oct 20-21, 2026. TI usually reports on the Tuesday of the third or fourth week of October; I am estimating that date, not quoting it. The Q3 guide was $5.65-6.15B in revenue and $2.23-2.57 EPS. Given the price increases and lead times a couple of weeks longer, Q3 itself will most likely land at or above the midpoint. The risk is the Q4 guide. Q4 is seasonally down, management has already flagged tariff and auto restock pull-ins, and depreciation keeps rising. The stock fell about 19% after a beat-and-raise in July (TIKR, 8/27) because it was priced for perfection, and it has since recovered from about $262 to $294. That pattern argues for a slight downside skew on the print, not a directional call. MOFCOM's anti-dumping probe was due by 2026-09-13 and could be announced or extended at any time. I use a lognormal with a $291.5 median (about 1% below spot) and roughly 12% monthly sigma, which is the 42% annual realized vol divided by 3.5.

fair_value.method: 60% P/E plus 40% FCF yield. P/E: 12-month-forward EPS at Oct-2027, about $11.15 (25% of CY27 consensus $9.84 plus 75% of CY28 $11.59), cut 7% to $10.37 for pull-in and peak-cycle risk, times 25x (peer CY27 median 23.8x) = $259. FCF: 2027E FCF about $7.8B on about 905M shares = $8.6/share at a 3.3% yield = $261.

inputs_detail.derivation: 0.25 x 9.84 + 0.75 x 11.59, the NTM window Q4'27-Q3'28 the market will price in Oct 2027

Management said some demand was pulled forward. Auto customers are refilling inventory from unsustainably low levels. A data center share gain came partly from rival foundry bottlenecks and could reverse. Depreciation rises again in 2027. Together these make consensus CY28 EPS (up 18%, only 5 estimates) more likely to be cut than raised.

Peer median CY2027 P/E is 23.8x (range 14.6-74.9x). 25x is a small premium, about 1x, for the Aa3 balance sheet and capex falling from roughly $5B a year to $2-3B, which lifts FCF conversion. TXN's own current 29.9x CY27 premium is not carried forward (see comps_summary).

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: 2027E FCF $7.8B / 905M shares = $8.6 per share at a 3.3% yield

inputs_detail.derivation: 2027 revenue of about $24.5B (2026 consensus $21.9B plus about 12%, in line with the EPS growth path) at about a 42% operating cash flow margin (TTM pace) gives $10.3B, less $2.5B capex. No CHIPS incentives are assumed.
Q2 diluted count of 920M less about 1.5% a year in net buybacks
Current EV of $275B against forward EBITDA implies about 25x. A 3.3% yield, about 30x FCF, gives credit for capex normalization but none for a further re-rating.

bear.story: The 2026 surge, with data center about 2x and an auto restock, turns out to be a pull-in or scarcity spike. Order cancellations start in 1H27 as rivals' capacity frees up. China puts anti-dumping duties on TI interface and gate-driver chips. Rising depreciation compresses gross margin back toward the mid-50s. CY28 EPS gets cut to about $9.3 and the multiple de-rates to about 21x, near the peer median, giving about $195.

base.story: Recovery continues but the growth rate slows. CY27 EPS lands around $9.8 and NTM EPS around $10.5-11. The multiple compresses from 30x CY27 toward 25-26x as the cycle matures. The dividend (about 2%) is the main part of the return.

bull.story: Industrial recovery, which is still about 15% below its prior peak, adds to data center power growth. Pricing holds, utilization rises with capex down, and FCF passes $9B. NTM EPS reaches about $12.5 at 30x.

comps_summary.peer_range: CY2027 P/E 14.6x (NXPI) to 74.9x (LSCC). Estimated CY2027 EV/EBITDA 8.3x (STM) to 128x (LSCC). The single basis for every P/E is calendar-2027 street EPS from the Nasdaq/Zacks consensus; off-December fiscal years (ADI, MCHP, QCOM, SWKS, QRVO, ALGM) were time-weighted to calendar 2027. Forward EV/EBITDA is an estimate: current EV divided by TTM EBITDA grown by each company's CY26-to-CY27 EPS growth ratio.
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: TXN trades at 29.9x CY27 EPS and about 24.8x estimated forward EV/EBITDA, a 26% P/E premium to the peer median. I apply 25x to horizon NTM EPS, about 1x above the median and inside the range.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: The case for a lasting premium is limited. TXN's CY27 EPS growth (16%) is below the median peer (about 21-30% for ADI, MCHP, NXPI and ON). Its revenue is just as cyclical, with a 2023-24 peak-to-trough decline of about 30%. It is also exposed to China anti-dumping action alongside ADI and ON. What does persist: Aa3/A+ credit, a 300mm cost position, and capex stepping down from about $5B to $2-3B, which structurally raises FCF conversion. I credit that with about 1x of P/E, not the current 6x.

thesis_break_reason: Below about $205, the stock would be at about 21x CY27 consensus or about 18x the horizon NTM EPS. That is under the peer median and close to my bear case. Getting there in a decent tape would most likely mean the market sees order cancellations or channel destocking (the pull-in reversing), a failing gross-margin bridge from rising depreciation, or punitive China AD duties. Ordinary 42%-vol noise around a $280 base would not usually reach it. It also sits below the August 2026 low of about $262 by a wide margin.

reasoning: Skeptic lane. The facts: Q2 2026 revenue was $5.46B (+23% YoY), EPS $2.14 and gross margin 61%, and the Q3 guide is $5.65-6.15B with EPS of $2.23-2.57 [1]. Street CY27 EPS is $9.84 and CY28 is $11.59 [2], so at $293.8 the stock trades at 29.9x CY27. The 12 analog and mixed-signal peers trade at a 23.8x median on the same calendar-2027 basis [2,3,4]. The bear evidence: (a) management and independent analysis both say part of the 2026 surge is auto restocking from unsustainable lows and tariff or bottleneck pull-ins [6,7,17]. (b) Depreciation is rising into 2027 [17]. (c) Goldman, Mizuho and Morgan Stanley have argued over-built capacity and an unjustified premium [14,15,16]. (d) China's AD probe names TI explicitly [11,12]. (e) The CFO sold about $26M on his way out and the CEO sold $5.6M near $280 [9,10]. That is option-exercise selling, which is weak evidence, but none of the insider activity was buying. Counterweights: Aa3/A+ credit with modest net debt (about $7B: $14B debt less $7B cash) [1,13], channel inventories that look lean, not stuffed [7], a mean sell-side target of about $325 [5], and estimates that rose through August even as the stock fell [8]. A modest premium valuation gives a fair value of about $260, or $259 with a 7% skeptic EPS haircut at 25x. A 2026 FCF-yield cross-check gives $261. For the ladder I put the median at about $283, between fair value and spot plus the dividend, rather than on fair value. Sell-side momentum and a still-rising cycle in early 2027 argue against a full move to fair value. Dispersion uses a lognormal sigma of about 37%. That is a bit under the 42% realized vol, which was inflated by the 2026 run-up and the drawdown that followed, and it is consistent with ±30-35% large-cap base rates. Scenario weights 25/50/25 at $195/$280/$375 give a mean of about $283, consistent with the ladder. Research limits: Twelve Data and Alpha Vantage were plan- or rate-limited, so peer EV/EBITDA is an estimate, not a consensus EBITDA figure. The Q3 report date and the AD ruling status could not be confirmed.
